description: A4 PBO-tie golden fixture — the PBO rank tie-direction must treat a degenerate all-tie OOS as OVERFIT, not as not-overfit. compute_pbo ranks the IS-best config OOS via `rank_c = sum(1 for s in oos_scores if s <= is_best_oos)` (math_engine.py:1960). On an ALL-TIE OOS (every config scores identically) the `<=` counts every config -> rank_c = K -> omega_bar = (K-0.5)/K ~ 1 -> lambda > 0 -> NOT counted as overfit -> PBO -> 0 ('robust'). That is the optimistic tie direction: a degenerate strategy that distinguishes nothing OOS reads as maximally robust. The fix changes `<=` to `<` (strict): rank_c = 0 -> omega_bar ~ 0 -> lambda < 0 -> counted -> PBO -> 1 ('overfit').
citation: Bailey & Lopez de Prado 2014, DOI 10.21314/JCF.2014.005; validation/overfitting.md PBO-tie; GATE2-PLAN A4.
provenance: Hand-authored degenerate-tie config set (all configs identical -> every IS and OOS score equal). The pre-fix and post-fix PBO values (0.0 and 1.0) are STRUCTURAL endpoints of the tie convention, not SUT-derived literals: 0.0 = optimistic (current), 1.0 = pessimistic/overfit (fixed). The test asserts the post-fix value indicates overfit (PBO > PBO_REJECT_THRESHOLD) without pinning an exact float beyond the structural endpoint.

all_tie_oos_is_overfit.description: All configs identical -> every IS/OOS score ties. After the strict-tie fix the PBO must indicate OVERFIT (PBO == 1.0, and > PBO_REJECT_THRESHOLD). Pre-fix it is 0.0 (RED).
all_tie_oos_is_overfit._assertion_kind: decision — post-fix PBO indicates overfit (== 1.0 and > PBO_REJECT_THRESHOLD). RED pre-fix (== 0.0).

non_tie_golden_unaffected.description: Regression: a clearly-dominant config (config 0 best every day) must keep PBO == 0.0 under BOTH tie conventions (no all-tie OOS, so the <= vs < change is a no-op). Pins that the tie fix does NOT change the non-degenerate case.
non_tie_golden_unaffected._assertion_kind: regression — PBO == 0.0 (config 0 dominates IS and OOS; no tie). Unchanged by the <= -> < fix.
